questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Give a short account on the structure of viral envelope.
questions.modelAnswer: The viral envelope is a lipoprotein membrane surrounding some viruses. Its lipid component is acquired from host-cell membranes during budding, making enveloped viruses more sensitive to heat and detergents; disruption of the envelope kills the virus. The glycoprotein component is virus-specific, attaches to host-cell receptors, and is antigenic, stimulating humoral immune responses.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: Mention the mechanism of cell tropism.
